walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethics: Issues of Human Life & Death / Animal Life & Death — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ethics: Issues of Human Life & Death / Animal Life & Death brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ethics: Issues of Human Life & Death / Animal Life & Death.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Platonic dialogue, set on the day of Socrates' execution, presents his main arguments for the immortality of the soul?
options: Republic
Phaedo
Symposium
Apology

mcqs.q: Which doctrine is Catholic and Protestant disagreement on?
options: Resurrection
Purgatory
Trinity
Incarnation

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.

mcqs.q: Bentham's famous test for the moral status of animals was:
options: 'The question is not, Can they reason? nor, Can they talk? but, Can they suffer?'
whether animals possess immortal souls
whether animals can enter into contracts
whether animals are made in the image of God

mcqs.q: A Kantian argues we should not be cruel to animals primarily because:
options: cruelty to animals damages our moral character and our duties to humanity — an indirect duty
animals are rational ends in themselves
animal suffering outweighs human pleasure in the calculus
scripture forbids the mistreatment of animals

mcqs.q: The doctrine of double effect would permit a doctor to give pain relief that foreseeably shortens a patient's life only if:
options: the intention is to relieve pain, death is an unintended side-effect, and there is proportionate reason
the patient's death is the means by which suffering is ended
the doctor believes death would benefit the hospital
the patient's family consents to euthanasia

mcqs.q: The view that human life has inviolable worth because humans are made in the image of God is known as:
options: the sanctity of life
the quality of life argument
personism
speciesism
